## Handoff — Alder Glen Permits Online v4.2 ACR draft (agp-2026c2)

**This is a DRAFT for human review and sign-off. It is not a final ACR, it is not signed, and it makes no conformance claim on the City's behalf.**

### Finish surface

Catalog `2.4-edition-wcag-2.1-508-en`, selected at planning time from the engagement's report-template requirement — the City's procurement office completes and signs in **GSA's ACR Editor (https://acreditor.section508.gov/)**, which cannot import WCAG 2.2-catalog documents today.

Open the editor → **"Open report"** → select the YAML. The editor validates on import, renders the chapter notes, and drops the four `disabled:` Section 508 chapters from its progress meter. Everything is stored in your browser's localStorage only — **nothing is uploaded to a server, and the saved YAML file is the persistence mechanism.** Export when done.

### Draft status: COMPLETE — no INCOMPLETE gate triggered

All 50 catalog A/AA criteria (30 Level A + 20 Level AA) carry a term. **Zero untested, zero `cantTell`**, so the document `notes` correctly carry no `INCOMPLETE DRAFT` marker and no criteria were omitted. `not-evaluated` appears in the AAA chapter only.

Term distribution (as rendered by the CLI): Level A — 22 supports / 1 partially-supports / 1 does-not-support / 6 not-applicable. Level AA — 18 supports / 2 not-applicable. Level AAA — 28 not-evaluated.

### Read this before the document goes to procurement

**1.1.1 will be misread, and you should decide what to do about it.** The term is `does-not-support`, correctly derived from the outcome (failed in all 9 samples, because the defect sits in the sitewide header template). But the catalog's own definition of that term is a *functionality-proportion* claim — "the majority of product functionality does not meet the criterion" — while our evidence is *sample-scoped*, and the actual impact is MINOR: one decorative-image alt string announced once per page, with content and controls unaffected. A procurement reader who reads the term against the catalog definition will conclude something much worse than what was measured. The note carries the sample scope and the impact explicitly so the claim's basis is visible; you may want to reinforce that in the chapter note or in a cover letter. **Do not "fix" this by softening the term** — severity never selects the term, and the fix is remediation (one template change resolves the whole row), not relabeling.

**2.2.1 is a `supports` row with a CRITICAL finding in its history.** The cycle-1 session-timeout defect was remediated in v4.2 and re-verified absent this cycle, so the measured cycle-2 outcome is `passed` and the term is `supports`. Per the evidence contract, no `finding_id` is cited on a passing check; the resolved-trend context is in the note without one. If a reader asks why a CRITICAL finding does not appear in the ACR, that is the reason.

**4.1.1 Parsing exists in this document only because of the finish surface.** WCAG 2.2 removed it; it is in the 2.1 catalog, so the team evaluated it specifically for this draft (automated parsing checks across all samples). It is not part of the WCAG 2.2 AA target that was actually measured.
